about/adaptive-training.title: Adaptive Training System
about/adaptive-training.description: Surogate includes a built-in adaptive training system that monitors your training run in real time and provides actionable diagnostics. It detects problems like loss plateaus, gradient explosions, MoE routing collapse, and inefficient compute usage — then tells you exactly what to fix.

about/automatic-differentiation.title: Automatic Differentiation
about/automatic-differentiation.description: Surogate's DSL includes a powerful Ahead-Of-Time (AOT) automatic differentiation system that derives backward computation graphs from forward graphs. This enables automatic gradient computation for training without manually implementing backward passes.

about/how-it-works.title: How Surogate Works
about/how-it-works.description: Surogate is designed from the ground up for maximum throughput and efficiency when training Large Language Models (LLMs) on modern NVIDIA hardware. Unlike many frameworks that rely heavily on high-level abstractions which introduce overhead, Surogate bridges the gap between Python's flexibility and CUDA's raw performance with a DSL-driven compiler pipeline.

appendix/compatibility.title: Compatibility
appendix/compatibility.description: This page summarizes practical compatibility constraints for typical installs.

appendix/release-notes.title: Release notes
appendix/release-notes.description: Use the GitHub Releases page to get the latest release notes.

develop/features/agents.title: Agents
develop/features/agents.description: The Agents page (Develop mode) is the densest screen in the platform. Every knob here changes how your agent behaves.

develop/features/browser.title: Agent browser
develop/features/browser.description: Give an agent a real, session-scoped Chromium browser it can drive — navigate, read the page, click, type, scroll, and screenshot — while you watch live and take over when a human step is required.

develop/features/browser-profiles.title: Browser profiles
develop/features/browser-profiles.description: A browser profile is a saved, encrypted browser login that an agent can reuse, so it stays signed in to a site across sessions instead of logging in every time.

develop/features/byo-llm.title: BYO LLM
develop/features/byo-llm.description: When the BYO LLM toggle is on, the platform routes LLM calls through your own provider instead of Surogate's bundled endpoints. Surogate charges only for platform usage (storage, compute, sessions); your provider charges for tokens.

develop/features/compute.title: Compute
develop/features/compute.description: The Compute page is where you wire up GPU providers so the platform can run training jobs, serve fine-tuned models, and drive data pipelines on your behalf. You don't manage Kubernetes or VM provisioning — the platform does that — but you choose which provider runs what, and you watch everything that's consuming compute in one place.

develop/features/connect-compute.title: Connect compute
develop/features/connect-compute.description: The Compute page is where you wire up cloud GPU providers, watch what's running, and set scaling policies. This page walks through the onboarding — the tabs, connecting a provider, and browsing the instance types a backend offers. For the conceptual overview of why and when to connect a provider, see Compute.

develop/features/datasets.title: Datasets
develop/features/datasets.description: A dataset is a versioned corpus you use for training and evaluation. Every dataset is backed by a repository in the Data Hub — the training files (train/dataset.parquet, plus a dataset_dict.json split manifest) live there, while the dataset's metadata (name, format, status, stats, PII scan, pipeline) lives in the platform database. Creating, building, and deleting datasets all go through /api/datasets.

develop/features/evaluations.title: Evaluations
develop/features/evaluations.description: Evaluations test models and agents against benchmarks. Two paths: pick from the 40 built-in benchmarks, or build a Custom Benchmark.

develop/features/hub.title: Data Hub
develop/features/hub.description: The Data Hub is Git for data. Every artifact your project produces — a skill, a dataset, a model, a knowledge base, a training experiment — is stored as its own versioned repository with branches, commits, and tags. The Hub is backed by surogate-hub, a lakeFS-based object store, so a repo behaves like a git repo whose objects happen to be data files instead of source code.

develop/features/knowledge-bases.title: Knowledge Bases
develop/features/knowledge-bases.description: A KB is a curated corpus the agent can browse at runtime via kblistpages / kbreadpage. Where a skill teaches the agent how to do something, a KB tells it what it knows.

develop/features/mcp-and-vault.title: MCP & Vault
develop/features/mcp-and-vault.description: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting LLMs to external tools and data. Surogate ships a full MCP client + a credential-injecting proxy + security scanning.

develop/features/media-generation.title: Media generation
develop/features/media-generation.description: Agents can generate images and videos through two built-in tools:

develop/features/memory.title: Agent memory
develop/features/memory.description: Agents keep a small, curated store of durable facts that survives across sessions, so a user never has to repeat themselves.

develop/features/models.title: Models
develop/features/models.description: The Models page is where you register and serve the LLM endpoints your agents call. Click DEPLOY MODEL at the top of the page to open the deploy flow: first a source picker, then a per-source form, then the model's detail page where you configure and start it.

develop/features/playground.title: Playground
develop/features/playground.description: The Playground is an interactive chat where you send prompts to a model that is currently serving and watch it stream a reply live. Use it to sanity-check a model or a fine-tune before you wire it into an agent.

develop/features/sessions.title: Sessions
develop/features/sessions.description: Every conversation is a session, fully recorded and inspectable. This chapter is about reading and using session data deliberately — what to look at, what to filter on, what to extract for training and evaluation.

develop/features/skill-optimization.title: Skill optimization
develop/features/skill-optimization.description: Skill optimization automatically searches for a better SKILL.md for one of your skills. It runs the skill against a target agent, reflects on where it fell short, proposes edited candidates, scores them, and keeps the best. The live skill is never changed until you explicitly apply a candidate.

develop/features/skills-and-experts.title: Skills & Experts
develop/features/skills-and-experts.description: The Skills & Tools page (in Work mode's nav) has two tabs — SKILLS and MCP SERVERS; this chapter is the builder's deep dive into both. A skill is a markdown file (SKILL.md) the agent loads into its prompt. An expert is a skill whose type is expert — backed by a fine-tuned model that runs in a bounded mini-loop.

develop/features/training.title: Training
develop/features/training.description: The Training page launches fine-tuning runs. Two methods can be created and launched from Studio — SFT and GRPO — each with their own configuration.

develop/intro.title: Welcome to Develop mode
develop/intro.description: For designing agents, writing skills, training experts, running evaluations, integrating via API, and deploying on your own cluster. Flip to Work mode in the navbar if you only need to chat with deployed agents and watch sessions.

develop/loop/build.title: Build phase
develop/loop/build.description: Everything you declare about the agent before users start using it: its identity, its tool envelope, what data it can search, where it's reachable, how governance constrains it.

develop/loop/observe.title: Observe phase
develop/loop/observe.description: Sessions are your source of truth. Every conversation, tool call, LLM response, and governance decision is in the event log. This chapter is about reading that data with intent.

develop/loop/overview.title: The builder loop (overview)
develop/loop/overview.description: Every agent improvement cycle has four phases:

develop/loop/redeploy.title: Redeploy phase
develop/loop/redeploy.description: Config changes are cheap. Model changes are slightly more involved. The runtime is built so neither drops traffic.

develop/loop/train.title: Train phase
develop/loop/train.description: You have a corpus of marked sessions. Now use them to make the agent better.

develop/quickstart.title: Quickstart
develop/quickstart.description: Deploy a custom agent with attached skill + KB + scoped tool envelope, then call it from a Python script. ~15 minutes.

develop/reference/background-jobs.title: Background jobs
develop/reference/background-jobs.description: Work that outlives a single agent turn — asynchronous sub-agents, durable tasks, scheduled runs, and the platform sweepers that keep everything tidy.

develop/reference/coordination.title: Coordination & the board
develop/reference/coordination.description: How a session becomes a strict coordinator that delegates instead of doing the work itself, and how the fan-out of workers it spawns coordinate through a shared, verified board.

develop/reference/event-types.title: Event types
develop/reference/event-types.description: The Sessions UI's EVENTS tab and the GET /v1/sessions//events API both return a stream of typed events. This page lists what you'll see and what each event tells you.

develop/reference/glossary.title: Glossary
develop/reference/glossary.description: Every Surogate term you'll encounter as a builder.

develop/reference/runtime-architecture.title: How the runtime behaves
develop/reference/runtime-architecture.description: The platform handles all the infrastructure — Kubernetes, model serving, sandboxing, policy enforcement. As someone building agents on top of ops.surogate.ai, you don't manage any of that, but a few behavioural guarantees matter when you design agents:

develop/reference/tool-catalog.title: Tool catalog
develop/reference/tool-catalog.description: Every built-in tool an agent can call. These are exactly the names the Governance policy accepts in Allowed tools / Denied tools — the catalog is generated from the runtime's real tool registry, and unknown names are rejected on save. (executecode and webcrawl are not tools; the shell entry point is terminal.)

develop/tools/copilot.title: Copilot (⌘+/)
develop/tools/copilot.description: The Copilot drives the platform itself on your behalf. Press ⌘+/ (Mac) or Ctrl+/ anywhere in ops.surogate.ai. For the operator's introduction, see Work mode → Copilot.

develop/tools/dashboard.title: Dashboard
develop/tools/dashboard.description: The Dashboard is the builder home at /studio — a dense workspace overview for monitoring agents, models, training, and recent activity.

develop/tools/templates.title: Templates
develop/tools/templates.description: The Templates page is a Work-mode surface (ops.surogate.ai/work/templates). In Develop mode the equivalent is the DEPLOY AGENT button on the Agents page — same dialog, same fields. Develop mode has no separate templates page.

develop/use-cases.title: Use cases
develop/use-cases.description: Seven multi-step end-to-end recipes for builders. Each one combines several Develop-mode features.

examples/grpo/grpo.title: Teach a model to reverse the prompt
examples/grpo/grpo.description: In this example we demostrate how to train Qwen3-0.6B to reverse a small chunk of text. We will use a SFT warmup to learn the skill of text reversal on longer documents and then a quick RL run to reverse smaller chunks of text in the reverse-text environment.

examples/index.title: Examples Library
examples/index.description: Surogate comes with a collection of pre-built training recipes and configurations for popular models and hardware setups. You can find these in the examples/ directory of the repository.

examples/pt/qwen3.title: Qwen 3 Pre-training (PT)
examples/pt/qwen3.description: This example demonstrates how to pre-train a Qwen 3 model using Surogate's high-performance FP8 hybrid recipe.

examples/sft/qwen3-lora.title: Qwen 3 LoRA Fine-Tuning (SFT)
examples/sft/qwen3-lora.description: This example shows how to perform Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on a Qwen 3 model using LoRA in BF16 precision.

examples/sft/qwen3-qlora.title: Qwen 3 QLoRA Fine-Tuning
examples/sft/qwen3-qlora.description: Surogate supports various quantization backends for memory-efficient fine-tuning (QLoRA), including BitsAndBytes (NF4), Native FP8, and Native NVFP4 (for Blackwell GPUs).

examples/sft/qwen3moe-lora.title: Qwen 3 MoE Fine-Tuning
examples/sft/qwen3moe-lora.description: Surogate provides optimized support for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, including efficient expert parallelism and memory-saving techniques.

getting-started/quickstart-grpo.title: Quickstart: RL Training (GRPO)
getting-started/quickstart-grpo.description: This runs a GRPO reinforcement learning example. GRPO coordinates three components — an inference server (vLLM), an orchestrator (rollouts + rewards), and a Surogate trainer (policy gradient updates) — via a single command.

getting-started/quickstart-pretraining.title: Quickstart: Pretraining (PT)
getting-started/quickstart-pretraining.description: This runs a pretraining job using a YAML config.

getting-started/quickstart-sft.title: Quickstart: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
getting-started/quickstart-sft.description: This runs a small LoRA SFT example using a YAML config.

getting-started/training-modes.title: Training Modes
getting-started/training-modes.description: Surogate supports four practical ways to adapt a model:

guides/configuration.title: Configuration
guides/configuration.description: Surogate is driven by a YAML config file.

guides/datasets.title: Datasets
guides/datasets.description: Surogate supports multiple dataset formats configured under datasets (and optionally validation_datasets).

guides/long-context.title: Long Context Training
guides/long-context.description: When fine-tuning at very long sequence lengths (8K, 32K, 128K+ tokens), MLP intermediate activations become the dominant source of GPU memory consumption. The long_context option enables tiled MLP execution, which chunks the MLP computation along the sequence dimension to reduce peak memory usage.

guides/memory.title: Memory
guides/memory.description: This guide collects the main knobs that affect GPU memory use.

guides/metrics.title: Training Metrics & Monitoring
guides/metrics.description: Surogate provides comprehensive training metrics that can be logged to file (JSON), stdout, and external backends like Weights & Biases (wandb) or Aim.

guides/moe.title: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Models
guides/moe.description: Surogate provides full support for pre-training and fine-tuning Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. MoE architectures replace dense feed-forward networks (FFN) with multiple "expert" FFNs, where a learned router selects which experts process each token. This allows models to scale parameters without proportionally increasing compute.

guides/multi-gpu.title: Multi-GPU Training
guides/multi-gpu.description: Surogate provides robust support for multi-GPU training, enabling efficient utilization of multiple GPUs to accelerate model training and handle larger models and datasets. The framework leverages data parallelism techniques with optimized communication patterns to distribute the workload across available GPUs.

guides/multi-node.title: Multi-Node Training
guides/multi-node.description: Surogate supports multi-node distributed training using Ray for cluster management and NCCL for high-speed GPU communication. This guide explains how to set up and run training across multiple machines.

guides/offloading.title: Offloading in Surogate
guides/offloading.description: Surogate supports offloading model components to CPU or NVMe storage to optimize GPU memory usage during training and inference. Offloading allows larger models to fit within limited GPU memory by moving less frequently accessed data to slower but larger storage.

guides/optimizers.title: Optimizers
guides/optimizers.description: Surogate supports two optimizers for training: AdamW 8-bit and NorMuon. Both optimizers use 8-bit quantized state storage to reduce memory consumption while maintaining training stability.

guides/performance.title: Performance
guides/performance.description: This page is a work in progress. It will collect practical performance tuning tips and describe major optimizations implemented in Surogate.

guides/precision-and-recipes.title: Precision & Recipes
guides/precision-and-recipes.description: This guide helps you choose a precision setup (recipes and optional QLoRA) and explains how the dtype knobs interact.

guides/qlora.title: Quantized LoRA (QLoRA)
guides/qlora.description: QLoRA enables memory-efficient fine-tuning by quantizing the frozen base model weights while training LoRA adapters in higher precision. Surogate supports two modes:

guides/rl-environments.title: RL Environments
guides/rl-environments.description: This guide walks through building environments with the verifiers library, from simple single-turn tasks to complex multi-turn agents with tools.

guides/rl-training.title: RL Training (GRPO)
guides/rl-training.description: Surogate supports reinforcement learning fine-tuning via GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization). The pipeline coordinates a vLLM inference server, a GRPO orchestrator, and the Surogate trainer.

reference/benchmarks.title: Speed Benchmarks
reference/benchmarks.description: All numbers represent total TPS (Tokens per Second)

reference/cli.title: CLI reference
reference/cli.description: Surogate exposes a small CLI with subcommands for common workflows.

reference/config.title: Configuration Reference
reference/config.description: This section provides a comprehensive reference for all configuration options available in Surogate. Each option is described in detail, including its purpose, default value, and possible values.

reference/python-api.title: Python API
reference/python-api.description: Surogate’s primary Python API is exposed via the surogate._surogate extension module (nanobind).

work/channels/proactive.title: Proactive engagement
work/channels/proactive.description: Let an agent do more than answer when spoken to — build context from everything in a channel and, when it is confident it will help, reach out on its own.

work/channels/self-registration.title: Self-registration
work/channels/self-registration.description: By default, only users you create by hand under Users can sign in to one of your agents. Self-registration flips that: visitors land on the agent's login page, click "Continue with Google" (or sign up with email + password), verify their email, and walk straight into the agent.

work/channels/slack.title: Slack
work/channels/slack.description: Publishes the agent as a Slack bot. Users DM it or @mention it in channels. Same conversations as on Web — if Slack identities are linked to Surogate users, sessions are shared.

work/channels/telegram.title: Telegram
work/channels/telegram.description: Simpler than Slack — one bot token and you're up.

work/channels/users.title: Users
work/channels/users.description: The Users section on an agent's Configure page manages the people who chat with this agent through its public Web endpoint. These are distinct from your operator account (your ops.surogate.ai login).

work/channels/web.title: Web
work/channels/web.description: The Web channel is always on for every deployed agent. Once the agent is running, anyone with the URL https://.cloud.surogate.ai can sign in and chat. On monetized agents, the web app is also the one channel a buyer's package can never exclude — every purchase includes it.

work/channels/website-widget.title: Website widget
work/channels/website-widget.description: The Website widget embeds the agent as a chat bubble on your own domain — marketing site, SaaS app, customer portal.

work/channels/whatsapp.title: WhatsApp
work/channels/whatsapp.description: Puts the agent on a WhatsApp business number via Meta's official WhatsApp Business Cloud API. Conversations are one-to-one (no groups, no threads), and the agent only ever replies — it never starts a conversation.

work/intro.title: Welcome to Work mode
work/intro.description: Work mode is for the day-to-day of running agents — chatting with them, watching sessions, attaching skills and KBs, publishing to channels. If you write skills in code, train experts, or run evaluations, flip to Develop mode in the navbar.

work/library/integrations.title: Integrations
work/library/integrations.description: The Integrations page connects third-party services (via Composio) to an agent, so it can use tools like Gmail, Slack, GitHub, and more.

work/library/knowledge-bases.title: Knowledge Bases
work/library/knowledge-bases.description: A knowledge base (KB) is the agent's searchable library. Where a skill teaches the agent how to do something, a KB tells it what it knows.

work/library/mcp-servers.title: MCP servers
work/library/mcp-servers.description: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting LLMs to external systems — your CRM, your ticketing tool, GitHub, internal APIs, anything that speaks MCP.

work/library/skills.title: Skills
work/library/skills.description: A skill is a small markdown file (a SKILL.md) that tells the agent how to handle a specific kind of request. Think of skills as reusable mini-prompts — procedural memory the agent loads when a request looks relevant.

work/monetize.title: Monetize your agents
work/monetize.description: Charge end users for access to one of your public agents. You decide the price and what each purchase includes — usage, channels, capabilities, knowledge bases, tools, skills, even the model tier. The payment goes straight into your Stripe account; Surogate keeps a 5% platform fee per sale.

work/quickstart.title: Quickstart
work/quickstart.description: A working agent on your team's Slack in 10 minutes. No code, no setup.

work/reference/faq.title: Troubleshooting & known issues
work/reference/faq.description: Known platform bugs and non-obvious failure modes. Pure UI-orientation issues (where things are, what buttons do) are covered in the relevant chapters.

work/reference/glossary.title: Glossary
work/reference/glossary.description: Every Surogate term you'll see in Work mode, in one place.

work/settings/authentication.title: Authentication
work/settings/authentication.description: The Authentication tab holds end-user sign-in configuration for your active project, at /work/settings/authentication (shared with Dev mode at /studio/settings/authentication).

work/settings/profile.title: Profile
work/settings/profile.description: The tab opens with "Your account details, avatar, and connected tools." — the account fields sit in an Account details card with the action row (Save changes / Reset / Change Password) pinned in its footer.

work/settings/usage.title: Usage
work/settings/usage.description: The Usage tab shows what your project has consumed this billing period, how much of each wallet is left, and a breakdown per agent and model. It's the real-time meter behind your plan — no end-of-month surprises. Balances refresh silently every minute while the tab is visible.

work/tools/chat.title: Chatting with an agent
work/tools/chat.description: The chat is where you actually talk to an agent — type a message, watch it reason and act, attach files it can work on, and steer a turn with slash commands. This page covers the composer and the controls that live around it. Open a chat from an agent's left navigation or at /work/agents//chat.

work/tools/code.title: Coding agents (`/code`)
work/tools/code.description: /code runs a real vendor coding agent — Claude Code or Codex — inside the session's sandbox, working on the session workspace using your own subscription or API plan.

work/tools/commands.title: Slash commands
work/tools/commands.description: Slash commands are shortcuts you type into the chat composer to steer the agent's next turn — start a goal, force a compression, run a coding agent, kick off research, and more.

work/tools/copilot.title: Copilot (⌘+/)
work/tools/copilot.description: The Copilot is an AI agent that drives the platform itself. Press ⌘+/ (Mac) or Ctrl+/ (Windows/Linux) anywhere in ops.surogate.ai.

work/tools/deep-research.title: Deep research (`/deep-research`)
work/tools/deep-research.description: /deep-research  produces a cited research report on a topic. The agent hands the topic to a dedicated deep-research sub-agent that plans the investigation, searches the web, curates an evidence bank, and delegates to a research-writer sub-agent for the final write-up.

work/tools/goals.title: Goals (`/goal`)
work/tools/goals.description: /goal is a slash command you type in the chat composer. Use it when the agent should keep working until a specific outcome is reached — not just answer one question.

work/tools/inbox.title: Inbox
work/tools/inbox.description: The inbox surfaces items the agent has explicitly raised to you. If it's empty, no agent has called askuserquestion or asked you to complete an external action — that's normal.

work/tools/missions.title: Missions
work/tools/missions.description: The Missions page is a dashboard for every goal your agent is working toward — the runs you start with the /goal and /mission slash commands.

work/tools/scheduled-work.title: Scheduled work
work/tools/scheduled-work.description: The Scheduled work page lists the recurring runs an agent performs on a schedule — the loops you set up with the /loop slash command.

work/tools/sub-agents.title: Sub-agents
work/tools/sub-agents.description: The Sub-agents page is a catalog of the specialized helper agents your agent can delegate to — each a preset bundle of system prompt, tool filter, model, and iteration cap.

work/use-cases.title: Use cases
work/use-cases.description: Five end-to-end walk-throughs you can adapt for your own work. Each one combines several Work-mode features.

work/workflow/configure-agent.title: Configure your agent
work/workflow/configure-agent.description: The Configure page — reached from an agent's left navigation (/work/agents//settings?tab=...) — is the core agent-building surface: twelve tabs that control who the agent is, what it can do, which model runs it, and where people reach it.

work/workflow/governance.title: Governance & AI disclosure
work/workflow/governance.description: Every agent carries a governance policy — tool access, web & browser egress, and EU AI Act transparency — configured on Configure → Governance (see Configure your agent for the form itself). This page explains what the policy actually does at runtime, and how AI disclosure reaches your end users on each channel.

work/workflow/improve-agent.title: Improve your agent
work/workflow/improve-agent.description: Start from the signal: the agent's Metrics tab (Configure → Metrics) shows error rate, latency, and a Conversations — last 7 days card whose Flagged count (a policy denial, a crash, or a thumbs-down) is the fastest pointer to the sessions worth triaging.

work/workflow/review-sessions.title: Sessions
work/workflow/review-sessions.description: Every conversation is a session — fully recorded, replayable, and inspectable. Open the Sessions page to review what your agent did: when something looks wrong, or to find good examples for improving your agent.

work/workflow/run-agent.title: Run an agent
work/workflow/run-agent.description: Open an agent from Agents in the left nav, then click New chat in the agent's left navigation (between Configure and Inbox). The composer opens with a Send a message... field; you'll see Commands / Skills / Scheduled Tasks shortcuts above it and an Add button for attachments.

work/workflow/templates.title: Templates
work/workflow/templates.description: The Templates page is where you start a new agent — either from a pre-built template or from scratch.
